In this study, we report the morphological, agronomic and molecular characterization of a group of maize landraces typically grown in Northern Italy and used to prepare the traditional dish polenta. The combined approach supported the identification and characterization of each accession, the exploration of phylogenetic relationships, and the analysis of population structure. Our results, demonstrating the distinctiveness of the accessions analyzed, highlight the importance of their conservation and valorization. Their protection and reintroduction into local agroecosystems represent a strategic opportunity to strengthen resilient agriculture, promote short supply chains, and contribute to long-term food security under changing environmental conditions.
keywords: plant genetic resources for food and agriculture

title: Understanding the Mortality Trends in Patients With Ventricular Arrhythmias and Cardiomyopathy: A 25‐Year Retrospective Analysis From 1999–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ventricular Arrhythmias (VA) associated with Cardiomyopathy (CM) continues to be the major cause of death. However, a national longitudinal study examining mortality trends from these conditions is still lacking. This study assessed mortality trends due to these conditions among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2024. METHODS: An observational analysis of U.S. mortalities due to VA in patients with CM (ICD-10 I47.2, I49.0 and I25.5, I42 respectively), was conducted using CDC WONDER. Adjusted Mortality Rates (AAMR) per 100,000 calculated and trends were assessed by calculating Average and Annual Percent Change (AAPC, APC), using joinpoint regression stratified by year, sex, race, and region. RESULTS: From 1999 to 2024, 81,204 VA with CM-related deaths occurred with the overall AAMR declined from 2.54 in 1999 to 1.01 in 2024 (AAPC: -3.55%; p < 0.000001). AAMRs decreased from 1999 to 2007 (APC: -7.93), remained stable till 2022 (APC: -0.66), and dropped by 2024 (APC: -6.87). Men exhibited greater AAMRs (2.42) than women (0.68). Racially, the AAMRs were most pronounced in Non-Hispanic (NH) Blacks (1.97), followed by NH Whites (1.42), whereas Hispanics and NH Others experienced similar AAMRs of 0.97. Geographically, Delaware and the Western regions experienced the highest rates of mortality (2.2 and 1.53, respectively). Urban areas had higher AAMRs than rural settings (1.45 vs. 1.4) CONCLUSION: Although VA-CM mortality has declined over the past two decades, differences by race, sex, and geography remain, underscoring the need for targeted healthcare strategies.

title: Left to cope alone: how pregnant and postpartum women and their newborns manage extreme heat in coastal Kilifi, Kenya
journal: Frontiers in Global Women s Health
abstract: Background In coastal Kenya, high seasonal temperatures compound structural challenges that include intermittent water access, resulting in health burdens from extreme heat. Women can experience limitations in the coping strategies available to them for protecting their health and wellbeing from high indoor and outdoor temperatures. This paper, drawing on the Climate Heat and Maternal Neonatal Health Africa (CHAMNHA) study, aims to describe how mothers and their newborns in rural Kilifi cope with extreme heat in their daily routines. Methods This qualitative study draws on key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions with pregnant and postpartum women ( n = 22), mothers-in-law ( n = 19), male spouses ( n = 20), community health volunteers ( n = 22), as well as frontline health providers, policy influencers, and government stakeholders ( n = 16). Participants were recruited in Rabai and Kaloleni Counties in Kilifi, on Kenya's coast, during a season characterised by extreme heat and drought. Data were analysed using NVivo 12, applying a combination of inductive and deductive thematic approaches. Results Women described five main strategies for coping with extreme heat. These included reducing or removing clothing, seeking outdoor shade and fresh air, ventilating indoor spaces, bathing and drinking cold water, and reducing or rescheduling daily activities. These strategies were also adapted for infant care. Mothers reduced infants’ clothing, moved them into shaded outdoor spaces, bathed or sponged them more frequently, and used culturally familiar remedies to manage heat-related discomfort and rashes. These practices provided immediate but partial relief. Heat-retaining and poorly ventilated housing, unreliable electricity, water scarcity and contamination, and diminishing tree cover limited women's options. Some strategies also introduced additional risks. Sleeping outdoors increased exposure to mosquitoes and personal-safety concerns, while opening windows brought dust into homes. Expectations concerning modesty, women's domestic workloads, and appropriate newborn care further constrained coping and sometimes created tension with older household members. Coping therefore involved continuous trade-offs between short-term thermal relief and social, environmental, and health risks. Conclusion Pregnant and postpartum women in rural Kilifi manage extreme heat through individual and household practices shaped by cultural expectations and material constraints. These practices offer only temporary relief, increase caregiving demands and, in some cases, shift rather than reduce risk. Responsibility for adaptation therefore falls largely on women themselves. Protecting maternal and newborn health is likely to require heat–health guidance in routine antenatal and postnatal care, engagement of households and community actors, and investment in reliable water, cooler housing and shade.

title: Explainable deep learning framework for real-time insect pest detection in smart agriculture
abstract: Abstract Global losses of crop production due to insect pest infestations are estimated to be around 20–40% annually, which represents one of the highest threats to agricultural productivity, farmer livelihoods and food security. Current manual scouting is labor intensive, subjective and non-scalable, and many automated scouting methods suffer when they come to deal with different field conditions and offer little insight into decision making. To tackle these challenges, this study proposes Crop Protection in Smart Agriculture—Real-time Insect Pest Detection using Continual Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (CPSA-RIPD-CSTGCN), a unified and interpretable deep learning framework that combines the four synergistic components: (i) the Ensemble Transform Schmidt–Kalman Filter (ETSKF) for image preprocessing, including resizing, normalization, and noise suppression; (ii) data augmentation using rotation, flipping, scaling, shearing, and contrast adjustment, which enhances generalization and reduces overfitting; (iii) the Continual Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (CSTGCN) that jointly models the spatial dependency across crop regions and temporal evolution of pest dynamics to achieve robust feature extraction and classification; and (iv) the Revolution Optimization Algorithm (ROA) for hyperparameter optimization of CSTGCN weights to adaptively adjust the network. Further, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization is introduced to give post-hoc explainability as it shows regions that are relevant to the biological process and areas that are affected by pests. This framework was tested on IP102 benchmark dataset with 60%-40%-split train-test with 10 economically important classes of pests with 97% accuracy, 98% precision, 98% recall and 98% F1 score, mean ± 0.32% accuracy, across 5-fold cross validation. Among other baseline models, these results consistently outperform VGG16 (82%), InceptionV3 (85%), MobileNetV2 (87%), DenseNet121 (88%), EfficientNetB0 (89%) and task-specific models like EDCP-DIA-RNN(Early Disease and Crop Pest—Diagnosis/Detection using Image Analysis RNN) (94%), EPCY-TPA-ANN (Efficient Prediction of Crop Yield—Through Parameter Analysis ANN) (91%) and ICPM-ESA-CNN (Interactive Crop and Pest Management Enhanced Soil Analysis CNN) (90%). The results of ablation studies showed the solitary effects of each module of the Ensemble Transform Schmidt–Kalman Filter pre-processing and Revolution Optimization Algorithm optimization, and the confusion matrix analysis demonstrated high per-class reliability and only a small amount of misclassification, implying that the proposed method could be applied to real-time, large-scale smart agriculture deployments.

title: Reducing Uncertainty in Cradle‐to‐Farmgate Carbon Intensity for Feedstock Using Model‐Data Fusion
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofuel carbon intensity (CI) quantifies greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the biofuel supply chain, providing a transparent metric guiding renewable fuel policies and enabling market‐based mechanisms to reduce GHG emissions. In this study, we focus on the cradle‐to‐farmgate feedstock segment of biofuel CI, the portion attributable to feedstock production from cradle to farm gate and directly influenced by agricultural management decisions. We quantify field‐level cradle‐to‐farmgate CI of corn and soybean feedstocks by integrating a process‐based model ( ecosys ) with a life cycle assessment (LCA) tool (GREET R&D FD‐CIC). We first identified CI uncertainty sources at a “supersite,” a representative farm in Illinois with comprehensive GHG measurements, using a Monte Carlo sampling framework that varied soil properties, management practices, and plant trait parameters across plausible ranges to quantify each source's contribution to CI uncertainty. Unknown plant trait parameters were the largest CI uncertainty source for both crops, with fertilizer information also important for corn because these inputs affect yield, N 2 O emissions, and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. We revealed widespread field‐level variability in cradle‐to‐farmgate CI within the same county, demonstrating the need for field‐level assessment. This variability was most strongly associated with SOC change for soybean (total‐effect index, 38%) and N 2 O emissions for corn (43%). While inherent uncertainty is inevitable, we demonstrated that a Model‐Data Fusion (MDF) approach, which integrates observational data including in situ flux measurements and satellite‐based remote sensing to constrain model parameters with known processes, can substantially reduce cradle‐to‐farmgate CI uncertainty. Specifically, we used crop photosynthesis and yield data for plant trait parameter calibration, and incorporated tillage and cover crop information as model inputs, achieving a 41%–52% CI uncertainty reduction. This work establishes a CI quantification framework composed of process‐based models, an LCA tool, MDF, and satellite data, enabling scalable, cost‐effective, field‐level cradle‐to‐farmgate CI quantification across regions.

title: The Longitudinal Association Between Disability and Loneliness Among Older Adults in China: An Urban–Rural Comparative Analysis
abstract: Loneliness is a major mental health concern among older adults and has been increasingly linked to functional decline in later life. This study aimed to inform targeted care strategies by exploring urban–rural differences in the longitudinal association between disability and loneliness among older adults in China. Data were obtained from 6654 adults aged 60 and older across three waves (2016, 2018, 2020) of the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS). Disability was measured with Activities of Daily Living (ADL) scale, and loneliness was measured with self-report items. Cross-lagged panel models (CLPMs) were constructed separately to examine the longitudinal associations for urban and rural older adults. Rural older adults reported higher levels of loneliness than urban older adults, and older women reported higher levels of loneliness than older men. Loneliness predicted increased disability at subsequent waves in urban and rural older adults. Disability predicted increased loneliness at subsequent waves only among rural older adults, not among urban older adults. Disability and loneliness were longitudinally associated among older adults in China, with notable urban–rural differences. Integrated physical and psychological interventions are critical in rural areas, whereas strategies should prioritize early loneliness screening to prevent subsequent functional decline in urban areas.

title: Trends and disparities in sepsis-related mortality among patients with lung cancer in the United States: CDC WONDER 1999 to 2023
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with lung cancer are at increased risk of severe infection and sepsis because of tumor-related immune dysregulation, impaired pulmonary defense, and exposure to anticancer treatment. However, the long-term population-level patterns of sepsis-related mortality in this population in the United States remain poorly characterized. Methods Using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death public-use dataset, we performed a retrospective population-level analysis of sepsis-related mortality among patients with lung cancer in the United States from 1999 to 2023, stratified by sex, race and ethnicity, age, urbanization level, census region, and state. We calculated age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs), evaluated temporal trends using Joinpoint regression, and generated exploratory forecasts for 2024–2030 using an autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model. Results From 1999 to 2023, 94,073 sepsis-related deaths were identified among patients with lung cancer in the United States. The overall AAMR increased from 1.62 (95% CI, 1.55–1.68) in 1999 to 1.95 (95% CI, 1.90–2.01) in 2023 and peaked at 2.03 in 2016. Mortality remained consistently higher in men than in women, was highest among non-Hispanic Black individuals and lowest among Hispanic individuals, and showed marked age-related heterogeneity, with the highest crude mortality rate in those aged 75–84 years and the largest increase over time in those aged ≥ 85 years. Increases were more pronounced in rural and small to medium metropolitan areas than in large metropolitan areas. ARIMA projections suggested that mortality may remain near recent levels through 2030, with no clear evidence of a substantial decline. Conclusion From 1999 to 2023, sepsis-related mortality among patients with lung cancer in the United States showed no meaningful long-term improvement and remained characterized by marked demographic and geographic disparities. Higher mortality burdens were observed among men, non-Hispanic Black individuals, older adults, and residents of rural and other high-burden areas. These findings suggest that reducing sepsis-related mortality in this population will require stronger infection prevention, earlier recognition, and timely intervention across the continuum of lung cancer care, together with broader efforts to address disparities in healthcare resource allocation and health equity.

title: Reducing malarial transmission through Burkholderia gladioli production of arsinothricin in rice rhizosphere: Explains the ‘rice paddy paradox’
abstract: Malaria is one of the largest and most persistent medical challenges today. Here, we describe a possible approach to limit Plasmodium falciparum (P.f.) transmission. In areas of Oryza sativa (rice), water puddles collect to form breeding grounds for the Anopheles gambiae (A.g.) mosquito. Lands with no rice initially were agriculturally developed into excellent sources of rice. Many believed more rice paddies would lead to larger cumulative areas of breeding for A.g. mosquitos, increasing malarial transmission - but the opposite happened. That is, increased rice growth increased A.g. breeding grounds, however malarial transmission decreased, aka the ‘Rice Paddy Paradox’ (RPP). Some theorized, this was due to financial relief that resulted from growing rice well. They believed that rice sales meant more money, enabling the purchase of mosquito nets as well as other improvements in general health. These explanations did not explain the reversal of the RPP, which occurred as time passed. Agriculturally well-developed areas with high concentrations of rice conferred higher malarial transmission over time. We believe we have an explanation for the RPP phenomenon and which, when harnessed, could reduce long-term malarial transmission rates and simultaneously grow rice well. Burkholderia gladioli ( B.g. ) produces arsenic containing arsinothricin (AST) which is toxic to P.f. through inhibition of glutamate synthetase-1. Evidence exists that supports the lack of malarial transmission when B.g. predominates the A.g. midgut. We believe that the A.g. midgut microflora mirrors the microflora of wet soil– A.g. breeding grounds. When B.g. thrives in the soil, it alters the normal rice rhizosphere, one of the causes of Bacterial Panicle Blight (BPB), rice death. Here, more B.g. is present in the environment, more B.g. is generally available to integrate into the A.g. midgut, reducing malarial transmission - less malaria in areas where rice grows poorly. When rice is thick, thriving, and growing, B.g. is eradicated in the soil. This leads to reduced amounts of environmentally available B.g. , and consequent reduced B.g. in the A.g. midgut, causing increased malarial transmission. That is, areas well developed with rice in time lead to rice overgrowth and indirectly to increased malarial infections—RPP reversal. Overall, our hypothesis ties together a relationship between A.g. midgut microflora and its connection to environmentally amounts of B.g. When harnessed artificially, this represents an important method to reduce malarial transmission. This would improve survival for those most at-risk for death - pregnant women, children, those with HIV, and others.

title: The relationship between adherence to the Mediterranean diet, food literacy, orthorexia and food insecurity in pregnancy
abstract: The Mediterranean diet is one of the healthy eating models accepted worldwide and has been associated with beneficial health outcomes in pregnant women. This study was conducted to evaluate the adherence of pregnant women to the Mediterranean diet and to examine the relationship between the Mediterranean diet and food literacy, food insecurity, orthorexia and prenatal stress. In this cross-sectional study, a questionnaire including demographic information, Mediterranean diet adherence scale, orthorexia nervosa scale, Short Food Literacy questionnaire, Household Food Insecurity Access Scale and Prenatal Distress scale were applied to 300 pregnant women. 41.3% of the participants were undergraduate and/or postgraduate; 72.7% were unemployed; 54.0% had equal income and expenditures; 35.7% were experiencing their first pregnancy; and 41.7% were in their second trimester. It was found that 78.0% of the participants had high adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MD), 88.0% had adequate food literacy, 76.3% had orthorexia tendency and 21.1% had food insecurity (FI). Adherence to the Mediterranean diet was found to be negatively associated with FI and positively associated with orthorexia tendency and food literacy (p < 0.05). Food insecurity was positively correlated with ORTO-15 scores (r = 0.119, p = 0.039), indicating that higher food insecurity is associated with a lower tendency toward orthorexia. Furthermore, food insecurity was negatively associated with food literacy (r=-0.144, p = 0.012) and positively associated with prenatal stress (r = 0.383, p < 0.001). In addition, orthorexic tendencies and adequate food literacy significantly increased the likelihood of adherence to the Mediterranean diet (p < 0.05). Food insecurity, not dieting before pregnancy, and not exercising before pregnancy decreased the likelihood of high adherence to the Mediterranean diet (p < 0.05). It was observed that the majority of pregnant women have high adherence to the Mediterranean diet, adequate nutritional literacy, and a tendency toward orthorexia. Food insecurity is negatively associated with adherence to the Mediterranean diet and nutritional literacy; it is positively associated with orthorexia and prenatal stress. The Mediterranean diet (MD) is a globally accepted model of healthy eating. Adherence to the MD during pregnancy contributes to improved maternal and infant health. Food literacy (FL) can increase adherence to the MD. Orthorexia, defined as obsession with healthy eating, is a condition that can be seen in pregnant women and can negatively affect the health of mother and baby. Another factor that poses a risk for maternal and infant health during pregnancy is food insecurity (FI). In this study, the relationship between adherence to MD, FL, orthorexia and FI in pregnant women was examined. There is a positive correlation between food literacy and adherence to the Mediterranean diet, whereas there is a negative correlation with food insecurity. A positive correlation was also found between adherence to the Mediterranean diet and orthorexia in pregnant women. Adherence to MD is high in most pregnant women, FL is adequate. Pregnant women are prone to orthorexia and at risk of FI. Food insecurity has been found to be associated with adherence to the Mediterranean diet, food literacy, orthorexia tendencies, and prenatal stress.

title: Socio-environmental assessment of Aedes aegypti distribution and risk of chikungunya in vulnerable community
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, poses a major public health challenge in tropical regions. In Brazil, its incidence has increased, especially in socioeconomically vulnerable areas, where environmental conditions favor the proliferation of vectors. Our objective was to assess the socioeconomic and environmental vulnerabilities associated with the spatial distribution of a) Ae. aegypti and b) resident exposure to CHIKV in a low-income community. Identifying key exposure hotspots, our work improves our understanding of CHIKV transmission in informal settlements and facilitates community-based interventions to mitigate CHIKV risk. We monitored Ae. aegypti using ovitraps and conducted a serological survey from October 2021 to June 2022 in a vulnerable informal community in Salvador, Brazil. Blood samples and sociodemographic, household, and environmental data were collected from residents aged ≥5 years. CHIKV serology was performed, and spatial models using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation assessed vector distribution, seropositivity, and associated factors. Among 194 ovitraps, posterior estimates indicated higher egg counts in peridomicile locations (IRR = 1 .99; CrI:1.3 1-3.0 6); households experiencing food insecurity (IRR = 1.77; CrI: 1.05 - 2.99), properties with unpaved yards (IRR = 3.76; CrI:2.31 -6.18), and areas with greater garbage density (IRR = 1.25; CrI:1.01 -1.56). Among 888 participants, Bayesian spatial modeling identified factors associated with CHIKV seropositivity: elderly (OR= 2.24; CrI:1.16-4.35), uncovered brick walls (OR=2.29; CrI:1.16-4.55), the presence of yards, either paved (OR=2.06; CrI:1.30-3.00) or unpaved (OR=2.71; CrI:1.73-4.25), and self-reported mosquito sightings (OR=1.94; CrI:1.19-3.18). In addition, remotely sensed Land Surface Temperature (OR=1.33; CrI:0.98-1.83) and the spatial ovitraps egg counts (OR=1.14; CrI:0.87-1.52) were relevant variables. Our high-resolution study identified fine-scale vulnerabilities linked to both Ae. aegypti abundance and heightened risk of CHIKV transmission. Based on our findings, effective control strategies should not only focus on traditional methods such as enhancing basic urban infrastructure and services and promoting community awareness, but also target specific breeding sites around homes, address garbage accumulation, and consider the influence of micro-scale temperature variations. These results emphasize the importance of tailored, neighborhood-specific interventions to effectively reduce chikungunya transmission in high-risk communities.

title: Mediating role of depression and anxiety in the association between food insecurity and delayed TB diagnosis in Botswana: a cross-sectional study
journal: Journal of Health Population and Nutrition
abstract: Abstract Background Delayed tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis remains a major challenge to TB control in low- and middle-income countries, where it contributes to prolonged infection, higher costs, and increased drug resistance. Food insecurity is an important determinant of health among people with TB and may contribute to delayed diagnosis through economic, physical, and psychosocial pathways. Depression and anxiety have also been associated with both food insecurity and delayed TB diagnosis, suggesting that they may mediate this relationship. This study examined the association between food insecurity and delayed TB diagnosis and assessed the mediating roles of depression and anxiety for this relationship among people newly diagnosed with TB in Botswana. Methods We recruited 180 participants newly diagnosed with TB in Gaborone, Botswana. Food insecurity, depression, and anxiety were measured using the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale, PHQ-9, and Zung Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, respectively. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between food insecurity and delayed TB diagnosis. Mediation analysis using a counterfactual framework was conducted to assess the mediating roles of depression and anxiety. Results Among the 180 participants, 45 (25%) experienced delayed TB diagnosis. Participants with delayed TB diagnosis had higher mean scores for food insecurity (4.16 vs. 2.99, p = 0.11), depression (10.1 vs. 6.92, p = 0.001), and anxiety (37.1 vs. 33.9, p = 0.05). In the standard regression model, every one-unit increase in food insecurity was associated with 4% higher odds of delayed TB diagnosis (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.98–1.11, p = 0.22). Our mediation analysis found positive natural indirect effects through depression (OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02–1.10, p = 0.01) and anxiety (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01–1.08, p < 0.001). Conclusion Mediation analysis revealed that depression and anxiety may represent pathways linking food insecurity to delayed TB diagnosis. These findings highlight the importance of considering both socioeconomic and psychological factors in addressing delayed TB diagnosis. Further studies are needed to confirm these pathways.

title: Estimating determinants of market participation and its impact on the income of under-utilized vegetable farmers in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract Under-utilized indigenous vegetables (UIVs) offer considerable potential for improving rural livelihoods in Nigeria due to their nutritional benefits, climate resilience, and cultural importance. Despite these advantages, their contribution to household welfare remains limited because of weak integration into formal markets. In the context of increasing emphasis on inclusive agricultural commercialization, market participation represents an important pathway for enhancing the welfare of smallholder farmers. This study investigates the determinants and income effects of market participation among smallholder farmers cultivating UIVs in Southwestern Nigeria. Primary data were collected from randomly selected farmers participating in the Nigeria–Canada Under-recognized Vegetable Project (NiCanVeg) across multiple states and agro-ecological zones. A Linear Regression Model with Endogenous Treatment Effects (LRETEM) was employed to address selection bias and unobserved heterogeneity in estimating the impact of market participation on income. Descriptive findings indicate that market participants tend to be younger, more educated, and possess greater productive assets and savings than non-participants. Econometric results reveal that socioeconomic and institutional factors, including gender, age, education, asset ownership, livestock income, and cooperative membership, significantly influence market participation decisions. The findings further demonstrate that participation in markets exerts a positive and significant effect on farmers’ welfare outcomes. The study underscores the importance of strengthening market access mechanisms for smallholder farmers and recommends policies aimed at enhancing farmer cooperatives, improving access to market information, and promoting inclusive value chains to support the commercialization of UIVs in Nigeria.

summary_id.tujuan: Menganalisis determinan partisipasi pasar dan dampaknya terhadap pendapatan petani kecil yang membudidayakan sayuran indigenous yang kurang dimanfaatkan (UIV) di Nigeria Barat Daya.
summary_id.metode: Desain cross-sectional dengan data primer dari petani yang dipilih secara acak dalam proyek NiCanVeg, mencakup beberapa negara bagian dan zona agroekologi. Analisis menggunakan Linear Regression Model with Endogenous Treatment Effects (LRETEM) untuk mengatasi bias seleksi. Ukuran sampel dan periode pengumpulan data tidak disebutkan dalam abstrak.
summary_id.temuan: Partisipan pasar cenderung lebih muda, lebih berpendidikan, dan memiliki aset produktif serta tabungan yang lebih besar. Gender, usia, pendidikan, kepemilikan aset, pendapatan ternak, dan keanggotaan koperasi berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan partisipasi pasar. Partisipasi pasar berdampak positif dan signifikan terhadap kesejahteraan petani, meskipun besaran efeknya tidak dilaporkan dalam abstrak.
summary_id.keterbatasan: Tidak disebutkan. Dari desain, data cross-sectional membatasi klaim kausal; validitas instrumen dalam model treatment endogen juga tidak dijelaskan dalam abstrak.
summary_id.relevansi: Temuan tentang peran koperasi, akses informasi pasar, dan rantai nilai inklusif relevan untuk petani sayuran dan hortikultura kecil di Kalimantan Tengah. Pendekatan LRETEM dapat diterapkan ulang pada data survei petani Indonesia untuk menguji dampak partisipasi pasar terhadap pendapatan.

title: Constraints and opportunities in cluster-based farming in Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background In many developing countries, smallholders play a central role in the agricultural sector, and holding significant potential for agricultural growth and rural development. In Ethiopia, agriculture contributes about 37.57% to Et GDP and supports the livelihoods of most of the population. However, recent agricultural growth has not efficiently addressed persistent challenges of food insecurity, malnutrition, and rural poverty among smallholder farmers. To improve productivity and promote commercialization, the Agricultural Transformation Agency introduced cluster-based farming approach aimed at transforming subsistence farming into market-oriented production system. Despite its potential benefits, the adoption and expansion of cluster farming remain limited due to several constraints. Therefore, this study reviews the opportunities and constraints of cluster-based farming in Ethiopia from social, economic, ecological/environmental, institutional, and political perspectives. Methods This study employed a systematic literature review methodology. Relevant studies were identified through digital libraries, web sources, Ethiopian public university repositories, ATA government website and other academic databases. A keyword-based search strategy was used to identify relevant publications mainly covering the period from 2015 to 2026. Based on relevance to study objective, a total of 23 empirical studies were selected and analyzed. Results The findings indicate that cluster-based farming in Ethiopia provides several opportunities across multiple dimensions. Social opportunities include enhanced farmer-to-farmer interaction, knowledge sharing, and collaboration. Economic opportunities involve improved productivity, economies of scale, better market access, and increased bargaining power. Ecological opportunities include improved natural resource management and the potential adoption of climate-smart agricultural practices. Institutional opportunities arise from stronger partnerships and coordination among farmers, government agencies, and development organizations, while political support through national agricultural development strategies further promotes cluster initiatives. However, several constraints also affect the implementation of cluster-based farming. These include farmers’ resistance to collective approaches, limited economies of scale among smallholders, unfavorable agro-ecological conditions, weak institutional coordination, and political instability. Conclusions Cluster-based farming has the potential to transform smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia by improving productivity, commercialization, and rural livelihoods. However, its success depends on addressing key social, economic, ecological, institutional, and political constraints. Recommendation Prioritize should be given to improving rural infrastructure to better connect cluster farms with markets. Expand agricultural research, strengthening farmer training, and securing financial support for cooperatives are also essential. In addition, promoting pro-poor agricultural strategies, extending extension services and ensuring continuous government monitoring and evaluation are necessary to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cluster- based farming in Ethiopia.

title: Satellite LiDAR reveals patterns in water table depth and flood risk in SE Asia coastal lowland and peatland plantations
abstract: Agriculture in SE Asian coastal lowlands is vulnerable to inundation and associated crop production loss. Quantifying and managing flood risk, surface subsidence, and carbon emissions (in peatlands) requires an understanding of water table depth patterns and controls, for which no comprehensive data currently exists. Here, we present a dataset of 15,575 measurements of canal water table depth below the soil surface (CWD) in large-scale industrial tree plantations across the islands of Sumatra and Borneo, derived from ICESat-2 satellite LiDAR data. A pronounced relation is evident between CWD and land surface elevation, which applies equally in different regions, both in peatlands and mineral soil areas, and in oil palm as well as Acacia plantations. Mean CWD varies consistently across elevation zones, from −0.6 to −0.85 m for oil palm and Acacia plantations, respectively (i.e., ∼-0.5 – ∼-0.75 m in peat soil) where the surface is 5–9 m above global mean sea level, to ∼ -0.2 m at 1–3 m elevation near mean sea level. The area of industrial plantations in the 1–3 m elevation range alone, which likely has the highest flood risk, is 984,700 ha. Accounting for larger areas of smallholder plantations, and for areas at higher elevations with impeded drainage, the total area of lowland plantations likely experiencing regular flooding could exceed 2.8 million hectares. The close relation with elevation indicates that plantation water levels, especially in lowest-lying areas, are often controlled by landscape drainability conditions rather than management targets, and that optimum water table depths for production and peat loss prevention are not achieved over large areas. We propose that such difficult-to-manage landscape elevation controls on water table depth are considered in yield projections and land use planning, as well as fire and peat carbon emission reduction policies. Unproductive flood-prone plantations as well as peatlands with very low water tables may be logical priority targets for restoration planning.

title: Farming under fire: Conflict, displacement, and the collapse of food security in south Lebanon
abstract: Context Lebanon's agricultural sector and food systems are facing unprecedented pressures amid overlapping crises: economic collapse, climate change, and the 2023-2025 armed conflict with Israel. Objective This paper investigates the compounded impact of conflict-induced displacement and climate stress on rural livelihoods, agricultural productivity, and food security in South Lebanon-an area marked by strategic agricultural value and climate vulnerability. Methods Drawing on 29 in-depth interviews with displaced farmers, cooperative leaders, and food producers from conflict-affected areas such as Marjayoun, Nabatieh, and Bint Jbeil, this qualitative study uncovers key disruptions in agricultural infrastructure, local markets, and household food access. Interview findings are also triangulated with published secondary quantitative data (IPC, FAO, WFP, and World Bank assessments). Results and conclusion s: The findings reveal how displacement led to the abandonment of farms, loss of livestock, contamination of crops, and collapse of cooperative models, exacerbating existing economic and climate stressors like currency depreciation, water scarcity, unpredictable rainfall, and reduced yields. Gendered impacts, informal solidarity mechanisms, and persistent energy and input shortages emerged as critical themes. The study highlights the urgent need for an integrated recovery strategy focused on smart irrigation, climate-resilient crops, market reintegration, and financial support for smallholders. The analysis is guided by a conceptual framework that treats conflict-induced displacement and climate stress as interlocking drivers of livelihood erosion, market collapse, and food and nutrition insecurity, with gendered and refugee-specific vulnerabilities at the core. Significance As Lebanon faces a worsening food insecurity crisis, with 1.17 million people in IPC Phase 3 or higher, rebuilding agriculture is no longer a developmental luxury but an existential necessity for national food security.

title: Local traditions, customary institutions and agricultural downstreaming in Agrarian communities of Prabumulih, South Sumatra
abstract: Abstract This study examines how local traditions and customary institutions shape agricultural downstreaming in agrarian communities of Prabumulih City, South Sumatra. While downstreaming is often promoted as a strategy for value addition, market integration, and rural income improvement, empirical evidence on how sociocultural institutions mediate farmers’ capacity to adapt to these transformations remains limited. Using a qualitative case-study approach, this research collected data through in-depth interviews with 20 informants, participatory observation, and document analysis across five villages (Karya Mulya, Karang Jaya, Tanjung Telang, Muara Sungai, and Pangku) with strong agricultural potential. Data were coded and analysed thematically using QDA Miner 6, guided by Social Capital, Institutional, and Value-Chain Theory. The findings indicate that successful downstreaming depends on the comprehensive integration of production, distribution, and marketing, which local traditions, customary institutions, and cross-actor coordination strongly mediate. However, challenges persist in tripartite collaboration, where government support remains insufficiently integrated with local institutional arrangements, and gaps in market access constrain the economic resilience of farming households. The study contributes to agrarian sociology by demonstrating that downstreaming should not be treated solely as a technical or market-based intervention, but as a sociocultural process requiring institutional alignment, trust-based coordination, and context-sensitive policy support.

title: Harnessing Dairy Goats for Food Security and Climate Resilience in Sub-Saharan Africa: An Interdisciplinary Review of Nutrition, Genomics, and Policy Pathways
abstract: Dairy goats offer significant potential to enhance food security, promote climate resilience, and improve rural livelihoods in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), particularly within women-led smallholder farming systems. This interdisciplinary narrative review integrates findings from nutritional science, climate adaptation studies, recent genomic innovations, and policy analyses (2010–2025) to critically evaluate dairy goats’ roles in addressing persistent malnutrition and vulnerability to climate extremes. Goat milk provides vital macronutrients and micronutrients and can contribute to improved dietary adequacy. Compared with larger ruminants such as cattle, goats—particularly indigenous and locally adapted populations—often exhibit greater tolerance to heat stress, flexible browsing behaviour, and lower water requirements. However, these adaptive advantages vary widely among dairy goat breeds, with high-yielding temperate breeds generally showing lower resilience to climatic extremes than indigenous SSA ecotypes. In addition, the per-kg GHG emissions for goat milk are typically higher than those for bovine milk, although system-level benefits may emerge in drylands where goats fit local heat/feed constraints and where species mix and management differ substantially. Recent genomic advancements, notably genome-wide association studies and selection signature analyses, have identified candidate loci for thermotolerance, disease resistance, and milk yield. Near-term improvement is most plausible where breeding is anchored in community-based programmes supported by minimal identification and phenotyping, with marker use most defensible when validated within target populations. Despite emerging opportunities through microfinance and climate finance, especially for women-centric cooperatives, dairy goats remain underrepresented in national livestock and climate policies, and life cycle assessment data to support formal carbon–credit integration are limited. We therefore recommend dedicated funding to goat-specific extension and animal health, targeted gender-inclusive training, strategic investments in genomic and data infrastructure, and enhanced data collection for carbon accounting. Overall, the evidence synthesised here indicates that scalable dairy goat development in SSA is unlikely without the coordinated implementation of climate-smart management and delivery systems (animal identification and core recording), alongside context-validated genomic approaches (e.g., MAS or genomic prediction integrated within community-based breeding where reference resources and phenotypes exist) and targeted policy and financing.

title: Patterns of Value Chain Participation and the Commercialisation of Underutilised Leafy Vegetables: Evidence from Sekhukhune District, South Africa
abstract: Indigenous and underutilised leafy vegetables (ULVs) can contribute to rural livelihoods and food security, yet household participation in their production, consumption, and marketing varies substantially. This study developed a typology of ULV farmers and examined factors associated with market orientation in Sekhukhune District, South Africa. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 266 farmers. Production Participation Scores (PPS), Marketing Participation Scores (MPS), Consumption Participation Scores (CPS), and an Extension Service Index (ESI) were constructed from standardised indicators. Ward’s hierarchical clustering identified farmer typologies, with k-means clustering used as a sensitivity check. Cluster differences were assessed using ANOVA and Tukey’s post hoc tests, while Spearman correlations and Firth’s penalised logistic regression examined associations and predictors of market orientation. Three typologies were identified: Low-Engagement Farmers (34.4%), Subsistence-Oriented Farmers (36.8%), and Market-Oriented Farmers (28.9%). The solution showed good stability (bootstrap mean ARI = 0.785) and substantial agreement between hierarchical and k-means clustering (ARI = 0.734; 90.1% agreement). Market-Oriented and Subsistence-Oriented Farmers did not differ significantly in production (p = 0.954) or consumption participation (p = 0.988) but differed in marketing participation (p < 0.001). Market access was the only significant predictor of market orientation (OR = 18.81, 95% CI: 7.34–48.25, p < 0.001). Strengthening market access may enhance ULV commercialisation.

title: Traditional preservation practices of asala fish (Schizothorax spp.) among Himalayan communities of Darjeeling, India
abstract: Abstract Traditional fish preservation practices are an important part of the cultural heritage and food systems of the Darjeeling Himalayas. In this study, the traditional methods used by local communities to preserve asala fish ( Schizothorax spp.) have been documented. Data were collected from the 50 respondents over the age of 18 including fish farmers, hatchery operators, fish processors, traders, and household members engaged in fish production, preservation, and marketing. Structured questionnaires, in-person interviews, direct field observations, and photograph were used to collect the data. Snowball and purposeful sampling methods were employed to find respondents with relevant knowledge and experience. According to this study, drying, wrapping in banana pseudostem (BPS) and fermentation are the main steps in the traditional asala fish preservation process. Among these methods, drying was the most frequently used preservation technique. The duration of preservation varied depending on the method used and local storage conditions. Wrapping in BPS is a unique and locally distinctive preservation practice that helps maintain moisture balance. According to local practitioners, these methods reduce spoilage and allow temporary storage of fish products without refrigeration. The findings demonstrate the importance of indigenous knowledge in preserving fish, reducing post-harvest losses, and supporting household food security. Documentation of these traditional practices contributes to the conservation of the local cultural heritage and provides baseline information for future research on sustainable fish preservation and management of fish resources in the Dhajea Tea Garden of Darjeeling Himalaya.

title: Determinants of communities’ adoption and practice of soil and water conservation measures in the Jema Watershed, in the highlands of northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Natural resource degradation is a major environmental challenge that threatens ecosystem stability and rural livelihoods, particularly in developing countries such as Ethiopia. Although soil and water conservation (SWC) interventions have been widely promoted, their adoption and implementation remain limited. This study aimed to identify the key factors influencing the adoption and implementation of SWC practices. To achieve this, a household survey and key informant interviews were used. The respondents’ knowledge was measured using yes/no items, while perceptions and practices were measured using five-point Likert-scale items. The composite and mean score values were calculated, and the result values were categorized using predefined score intervals such as very low to very high. To assess the community’s perception, knowledge, and practice on SWC and to identify the key factors, correlation and multiple linear regression analysis were employed. The findings indicate that the majority of respondents achieved composite awareness and perception scores corresponding to the ‘good’ category (50–75% of the maximum attainable score), based on the predefined classification criteria. The correlation analysis indicates a strong correlation between community knowledge and perception ( r = 0.64, p < 0.05), knowledge and practice ( r = 0.83, p < 0.05), and perception and practice ( r = 0.69, p < 0.05) in the study area. The multiple regression results showed that access to training (β = 0.620), knowledge (β = 0.496), source of information (β = 0.416), and extension services (β = 0.336) were the most influential positive factors affecting SWC adoption. Perception also had a positive, though smaller effect (β = 0.108). In contrast, land tenure insecurity (β = -0.109), along with factors such as small farm size and greater distance to farmland, negatively affected the adoption of SWC practices. Overall, the study highlights that strengthening institutional support, improving access to training and information, enhancing extension services, and ensuring land tenure security are essential to promote sustainable adoption of SWC practices.

title: How much climate-smart agriculture is enough? A dose-response analysis of technology adoption effects on farmer welfare in Ghana
abstract: Climate-smart agricultural technologies (CSAT) are promoted to enhance agricultural productivity and strengthen resilience to climate change. However, limited empirical evidence exists on the effects of adoption intensity, particularly when farmers adopt multiple technologies simultaneously. This study examines the effects of CSAT adoption intensity on maize yield and household asset accumulation in Ghana using survey data from 2,151 maize farmers. A dose–response model with Heckman selection is applied to address potential selection bias and estimate the causal effects of varying adoption levels. The findings show that farmers’ education, access to credit, extension services, and perceived drought significantly influence both the likelihood and intensity of CSAT adoption. Results reveal a U-shaped relationship between CSAT adoption intensity and maize yield, where yields initially decline but increase as adoption intensity rises. On average, higher CSAT adoption is associated with a 21% increase in maize yield. Similarly, CSAT intensity shows a nonlinear positive relationship with household asset accumulation, with an average 19.5% increase in assets. The results also indicate heterogeneous effects across farmers. Overall, higher CSAT adoption improves agricultural productivity and long-term household welfare, highlighting the need to strengthen extension services, expand credit access, and raise climate risk awareness to promote sustainable agricultural development.

title: Food security-oriented optimization of rural settlements: coupling GAEZ and PLUS to address cropland productivity loss in Shaanxi, China
abstract: Rapid urbanization and rural transformation continue to reshape production and living spaces in rural China. Cropland occupation and reclamation resulting from rural settlement evolution may alter the spatial configuration and production potential of cropland, thereby affecting regional grain production capacity. In practice, China's cropland requisition–compensation balance has primarily emphasized quantitative balance, yet it has not adequately addressed the productivity losses resulting from the occupation of high-quality cropland and compensation with lower-quality land. This study develops an integrated framework to quantify this dual loss in both quantity and quality, and to optimize rural settlement layouts with a firm food security orientation in Shaanxi Province, China. We couple the Global Agro-Ecological Zones (GAEZ) model with the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model. The GAEZ model was first used to estimate cropland grain production potential (GPP), which was then innovatively incorporated as a core spatial driver into the PLUS model to simulate and optimize the distribution of rural settlements. Results show that 93.43% of new rural settlements were converted from cropland. The occupied cropland (OC) had a higher average GPP than newly reclaimed cropland (NRC), leading to a net reduction of 49.62 × 10 4 tonnes in total GPP. The GPP-informed optimization demonstrated a significant mitigation effect, reducing the net GPP loss by 7.19 × 10 4 tonnes and substantially narrowing the quality gap between OC and NRC. The framework provides a replicable tool for shifting the core of cropland protection policy from a simplistic area balance towards a more secure productivity balance, offering critical insights for food security-oriented spatial planning.

title: Translating Cultivated Land Multifunctionality Assessment into Differentiated Governance in Northeast China
abstract: Cultivated land multifunctionality plays an important role in balancing food security, rural development, and ecological sustainability. However, existing studies often remain fragmented, with limited integration of long-term functional evolution, interfunctional relationships, coordination, and governance-oriented zoning. Using multi-source data from 2000 to 2024, this study examined the spatiotemporal evolution, synergy–trade-off relationships, coupling coordination, spatial associations, and functional zoning of cultivated land production, social, ecological, and landscape functions in Northeast China. The results show pronounced temporal fluctuations and spatial differentiation. Landscape function maintained the highest overall level, with a mean of approximately 0.82, while ecological function remained relatively high and stable. Production function fluctuated over time, whereas social function increased markedly in 2020 before declining slightly in 2024. Synergies dominated among production, ecological, and landscape functions, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.54 to 0.97, while social function remained weakly associated with the other functions (r < 0.22). The coupling coordination degree ranged from 0.639 to 0.665, indicating a moderate but relatively stable coordination level with clear regional differences. Functional zoning identified single-function-dominated, dual-function composite, multifunctional composite, and characteristic agricultural zones, accounting for 53.44%, 21.30%, 8.94%, and 16.33% of cultivated land, respectively. These findings provide a basis for shifting cultivated land management from uniform regulation toward differentiated governance that better coordinates agricultural production, ecological protection, and rural development.

title: Impact of Well-Facilitated Farmland Construction on Farmers’ Adoption Behavior of Improved Agricultural Machinery
abstract: Well-facilitated farmland construction provides a material foundation for the application of improved agricultural machinery, and the in-depth integration of the two can contribute to a new breakthrough in improving grain yield per unit area. Based on 371 farm household survey samples from Heilongjiang Province, this study employed the Poisson regression model, mediation pathway test model, and moderating effect model to explore the effect of well-facilitated farmland construction on farm households’ adoption behavior of improved agricultural machinery. The main finding shows that well-facilitated farmland construction can significantly promote farm households’ adoption behavior of improved agricultural machinery, and this conclusion remains valid after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. In terms of the heterogeneous impact of project types on adoption behavior, farmland road construction is the only type that generates a significant positive effect on adoption, while drainage facility construction and shelterbelt construction show significant negative effects; the other five types, including irrigation facility construction, gully erosion control, power facility construction, soil fertility amelioration, and farmland morphology remediation, have no statistically significant impacts. This study preliminarily identifies that the farmers’ organization level serves as a potential mediation pathway through which well-facilitated farmland construction facilitates farmers’ adoption of improved agricultural machinery, and both farmland fragmentation and poor traffic conditions exert significant negative moderating effects. In the future, machinery-oriented differentiated construction should be promoted based on local conditions, the farmers’ organization level should be improved, and targeted measures should be adopted to address farmland endowment constraints; this has the potential to further enhance the policy precision and implementation efficiency of well-facilitated farmland construction.

title: Integrated assessment of agricultural and processing-related chemical hazards across the food chain: glyphosate occurrence and lipid changes in ready-to-eat corn-based foods
abstract: Introduction Ready-to-eat foods may accumulate chemical hazards from both agricultural production and food processing. These hazards converge in the same food but are usually evaluated separately. This study assessed both types of hazard together in corn-based foods consumed on a Mexican university campus, as an integrated food-chain approach. Methods Ten tortilla and ten tortilla chip samples were collected from campus cafeterias and food stalls. They were screened for glyphosate by high-performance liquid chromatography with diode-array detection (HPLC-DAD), as an indicator of agricultural chemical hazards. Dietary exposure was estimated with a conservative upper-bound scenario and expressed as a hazard quotient (HQ) relative to the acceptable daily intake (ADI). Six paired frying-oil samples, collected before and after frying, were analyzed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to estimate iodine value (IV) as an indicator of lipid unsaturation. Results Glyphosate signals were detected in 8/10 tortilla and 10/10 tortilla chip samples (90% overall). Screening-level concentrations ranged from 0.107 to 1.994 mg kg −1 . Detected concentrations were above the Mexican maximum residue limit (MRL) for corn grain (0.1 mg kg −1 ) and below the Codex Alimentarius MRL for maize (5 mg kg −1 ); both limits were used only as regulatory reference points. HQ values were 0.0573 for women and 0.0511 for men, so estimated exposure was below the ADI under the assumed scenario. IV decreased significantly after frying (mean decrease 5.00 units; 95% CI 1.30–8.71; p = 0.0178). Discussion Ready-to-eat corn-based foods may carry both agricultural residues and processing-related lipid changes. HQ < 1 does not imply absence of risk. The frequent detection of glyphosate supports continued monitoring and confirmatory analysis by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). This integrated approach can support food safety surveillance in institutional food environments.

title: Illuminating gendered pathways: Exploring energy service demands in rural and peri-urban Nigeria
abstract: Gender gaps in energy access are well documented, but evidence on who prioritises which electrical appliances and why remains limited. This paper investigates links between appliance needs, gender roles, and intra-household decision-making in rural and peri-urban Nigeria. Using a mixed-methods design, it combines individual interviews and focus group discussions with a household survey (n = 3599). Qualitatively, appliance priorities are examined together with user values — via the User Perceived Value Game — to understand what appliances mean in everyday life. Quantitatively, appliance ownership is analysed using logistic and conditional logistic regression models, linked to a measure of women’s decision-making within the household. Women and men show substantial overlap in high-priority appliances, with mobile phones, fans, and televisions consistently ranking at the top. At the same time, systematic divergences emerge, with women placing greater emphasis on fridges and blenders, whereas men prioritise radios and torches. Group deliberations mirror these patterns but also reveal how group gender composition can mute gender-specific preferences. Value narratives indicate a largely shared set of values across genders, with device-specific differences partly shaped by gender roles. Finally, higher women’s decision-making power is positively associated with ownership of selected appliances, most robustly fridges and mechanical appliances, while local infrastructure and norms appear to condition whether decision-making power translates into ownership. The findings show women’s agency in shaping household energy priorities, but also the constraints that limit whether these priorities translate into ownership. This underscores the need for gender-responsive energy interventions. • Mixed-method evidence on gendered appliance priorities in Nigeria. • Device needs overlap, but women rank fridges & blenders higher, men radios & torches. • Gender composition of group discussions can mute gender-specific needs. • Women’s decision-making power is linked with fridge and mechanical device ownership. • Energy interventions should be paired with efforts to open up gender norms.

title: Becoming a ‘Chinese wife’: digital subjectivity, platform geopolitics, and the aesthetics of Ugandan influencer Rose Adikin’s media ecology
abstract: Digital media is the latest form of global communication, enabling political, economic, and cultural interactions at the macro level while simultaneously mediating these encounters into micro-level inter-user engagements. This paper argues that digital media platforms register and reinforce disparities of race, gender, and geopolitics within the ostensibly mundane practices of everyday content production and consumption. This paper focuses on the figure of the ‘digital subject’ that emerges on digital platforms – specifically, influencers who exploit platform logics to construct an online persona while subtly negotiating existing stereotypes to attract audiences and generate profit. I examine the case of social media influencer Rose Mary Adikin, a Ugandan woman who married a Chinese man and moved to Zhejiang, China. Her videos construct an image of everyday life as a rural ‘Chinese wife’, yet they also leverage the spectacular tension between her performance of ‘Chineseness’ and her racialised Black body, the asymmetrical gender dynamics within her household, and her shifting personas across different platforms. The gaps between Rose’s visible performance as a typical Chinese rural housewife and the invisibilized aspects of her African origins are constitutive of her digital subjectivity. Far from signalling a failure in self-representation, these gaps generate a unique pleasure in witnessing a mimicry that is ‘almost the same, but never fully Chinese’. The construction of digital subjectivity in her videos, and the constitutive gaps embedded within them, illuminate the complex mechanisms shaping Africa–China dynamics in popular visual culture, shedding light on the paradoxical nature of online self-representation, which simultaneously reflects and responds to the desires of others.

title: Rural occupational health in Colombia: policy–practice gaps among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca
abstract: This study examines policy–practice gaps in occupational safety and health (OSH) protection among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca, Colombia. A multi-method design combined 14 semi-structured interviews and two focus groups with an adapted ILO Vision Zero Fund survey administered to 200 agricultural workers. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and through exploratory Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), and qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated during interpretation. Findings showed multidimensional patterns involving occupational protection, working conditions, health-service availability, agricultural practices, and productive autonomy. These patterns coexisted with informal, seasonal, short-term, day-labor, and subsistence work, limited occupational risk coverage, discontinuous prevention and training, and fragmented institutional coordination. Qualitative findings further highlighted women’s combined productive and care roles, local and traditional knowledge, community participation, and heterogeneity across territorial settings and agricultural practices as relevant to prevention and decision-making. Conventional social protection and occupational risk arrangements centered on formal, contributory employment may not fully respond to dispersed and unstable rural work. Strengthening rural OSH requires integrated, territorially adapted, gender-sensitive strategies linking prevention, social protection, sustained training, institutional coordination, community participation, and productive autonomy. The findings support assessing differentiated and progressive protection pathways, including the feasibility of subsidized occupational risk coverage for more vulnerable workers and small productive units, combined with contributory mechanisms where work arrangements are more stable. By linking worker-level realities with institutional and policy-implementation gaps, this study provides evidence to inform more equitable rural OSH policies responsive to diverse territorial realities in Colombia.

title: Perceived Exposure and Vulnerability to Climate Risks in the Urban Centers of Zio Prefecture, Togo
abstract: Climate change and rapid urban expansion are increasing populations’ exposure to climate risks, particularly in secondary cities of West Africa. An analysis of local perceptions of these risks is therefore essential for improving the understanding of urban vulnerability and strengthening local adaptation and resilience strategies. This study analyzes the perceptions of exposure and sensitivity to climate risks in nine urban centers of the Zio prefecture (Togo), as well as their determinants. A mixed-method approach was conducted with 423 households, combining quantitative surveys and statistical analyses, including principal component analysis (PCA) and chi-square (χ2) tests. The results show that extreme heat (80.6%) and drought (66.7%) are the most perceived hazards, with significant spatial variations: drought is more frequently cited in small rural localities (90.2%), while floods and storms predominate in peri-urban areas. Women (up to 89.5%) and residents of risk-prone areas are identified as the most vulnerable groups. Factor analysis reveals two dimensions structuring perceptions: a chronic and economic component (income loss, migration, drought) and an acute hydrometeorological component (river flooding, human losses, storms). Remote rural municipalities (Zio 4) exhibit higher perceptions of chronic risks, while the peri-urban area (Zio 2) combines both chronic and acute risks. Housing and roads are perceived as the most vulnerable infrastructures. External support remained limited, with 67.6% of households reporting none; government assistance was the leading source overall (14.7%), while non-governmental organizations NGOs predominated in large settlements (30.0%). These findings confirm the intra-territorial heterogeneity of perceptions and highlight the need for differentiated, gender-sensitive adaptation policies that strengthen institutional alert and assistance mechanisms.

title: Employment effects of the Farmers to Families Food Box program on small businesses
abstract: Federal food distribution programs aim to address food insecurity while supporting farms and food businesses. Many of these programs include small business set-asides designed to improve outcomes for participating firms, yet little evidence exists quantifying their impact on small business performance. We study the Farmers to Families Food Box (FFFB) program, a temporary initiative operated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture from May 2020 to May 2021 that contracted vendors to assemble and deliver food boxes during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using vendor shipment records linked to firm-level employment data from the National Establishment Time Series, we evaluate whether participation in the program affected employment levels of participating small businesses. We estimate a Dynamic Two-Way Fixed Effect Difference-in-Difference model with matched treatment and comparison groups to test for effects on 2020 and 2021 employment levels while accounting for contemporaneous effects of the Payment Protection Program (PPP). Results show that FFFB participation was associated with higher employment among small businesses, with particularly robust evidence for positive effects in 2021. These findings provide some of the first quantitative evidence linking participation in federal food procurement programs to improved small business employment outcomes.

title: Circular economy assessment of biomethane value chain in Brazil
abstract: Abstract From the numerous opportunities to add value to biomass in Brazil, biomethane production in sugarcane mills presents significant potential. This study introduces a diagnostic framework grounded in circular economy (CE) principles to assess new biomethane projects, aligning with the strategic objectives of product diversification, full biomass utilization, circularity, and regional integration. By adopting seven CE principles to qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate systemic impacts, the assessment provides a flexible tool for visualizing and testing alternative biorefinery configurations during the feasibility stage. The framework is applied to two real‐world scenarios: (i) the on‐site replacement of diesel in agricultural and transport operations; and (ii) the regional commercialization of biomethane via pipeline to substitute industrial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Results indicate that both pathways achieve over 85% reduction in carbon intensity compared with fossil benchmarks, while simultaneously enhancing nutrient cycling and soil regeneration through improved digestate application. The CE‐based assessment further demonstrates that on‐site utilization fosters internal transactional efficiency and operational control, whereas regional distribution extends defossilization benefits throughout the broader industrial value chain. The framework facilitates strategic decision‐making by capturing dimensions of value retention, regeneration, and stakeholder collaboration within bio‐based systems. This approach serves as a replicable and complementary tool for evaluating diverse bioeconomy contexts, supporting the transition toward more circular and resilient regional systems.

title: Crop landrace conservation, status, challenges and motivations in Great Britain
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Recent agricultural intensification has led to the widespread replacement of genetically diverse crop landraces with high‐yielding but genetically uniform modern cultivars, reducing the adaptive resilience of farming systems. In the United Kingdom, where large‐scale agriculture dominates, landraces require urgent conservation action. This study provides the first comprehensive overview of landrace cultivation in Great Britain, examining current cultivation trends, why they are grown and the challenges growers face. By documenting these dynamics, this research provides evidence to inform conservation strategies and policy decisions that support crop diversity, resilient farming systems and genetic resources that could be used in future breeding programmes to ensure long‐term food security. Summary Landraces, genetically diverse crop varieties that have evolved through generations of saving seed on farm, are becoming increasingly threatened with extinction. In Great Britain, initial attempts to document landrace diversity are outdated and incomplete. This study reviewed crop maintenance trends and identified the major challenges and opportunities in contemporary landrace cultivation. Through farmer interviews, questionnaires and expert discussions, 197 landrace maintainers and 566 landrace populations have been identified on farm, with two diversity hotspots in Pembrokeshire and the Scottish Islands. A further 1876 landrace accessions of British origin were identified ex situ, contributing to a total of 1201 distinct landraces overall. The most common reasons for maintaining landraces were history and tradition, local environmental adaptation and market demand. Maintainer numbers and cultivation scale for cereal and vegetable landraces have increased since 2004; however, forage landrace diversity is becoming increasingly threatened. Across all crop types, the major challenges reported by maintainers were climate change, labour shortages and the lower yield of landraces compared with modern cultivars. Landrace cultivation should be valued, not just to safeguard historic plant genetic resources for food security but also to sustain ecosystem services and environmental health. More effective conservation strategies are required to overcome the challenges facing landrace cultivation and so ensure this potential resource exists to aid future generations in the fight against food insecurity and climate change.

title: Pacing and effort distribution in Hyrox® PRO athletes: differences by sex and performance level
journal: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: Hyrox ® has rapidly grown into one of the most popular High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT) competitions, combining running and strength-based stations in a comparatively standardised format. Although pacing and effort distribution are established determinants of performance in endurance sport and CrossFit ® events, no study has examined how these strategies differ by sex and performance level within Hyrox ® . This study aimed to characterize pacing and effort-distribution strategies among Hyrox ® PRO athletes and to determine whether they differ by sex and performance level. An observational, retrospective study analysed official Hyrox ® PRO results for 6,081 men and 2,341 women, the three fastest athletes were retained as a descriptive top-performance group, while the remaining performance groups were defined using z-scores of overall competition time. Relative time spent in each of the eight running segments and eight strength stations was calculated as a percentage of total race, running or strength time. Performance groups were compared using Welch’s ANOVA, sex × segment interactions using mixed-design ANOVA, and phase-by-phase sex differences across the race were tested using one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping (SPM1D), with Hedges’ g and partial eta squared (η²p) as effect sizes. Running pacing had a similar shape across performance groups, with small differences at kilometres 1, 2 and 8 (η² p ≤ .054). The SkiErg and RowErg accounted for a progressively smaller share of strength time as performance declined (η² p = .47–0.51), reflecting the disproportionate time lost by slower athletes at the loaded and bodyweight stations. Sex differences were trivial for running (η² p ≈ .005) but present at the strength stations in all performance groups (η² p = .060–0.098), with women devoting a larger share of time to the SkiErg, Burpee Broad Jump, RowErg and Farmers Carry, and men to the Sandbag Lunges and Wall Balls. Hyrox ® PRO athletes appear to share a common running pacing template, whereas performance differences concentrate in the loaded and bodyweight stations and sex differences in station time seem to follow the PRO category’s sex-specific load scaling. These findings provide a framework for developing pacing strategies adapted to athletes’ sex and competitive level.

title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. This study jointly examines the factors associated with the adoption of five common climate smart practices (i.e., crop diversification, agroforestry, integrated soil fertility management, small scale irrigation, and integrated pest management) among modern rice farmers in southwest Bangladesh, using a multivariate probit model. The analysis draws on 493 farm households randomly selected from complete household lists in three purposively selected villages, one in each of three districts spanning the region’s salinity gradient. Results show that adoption decisions are interdependent, and most households maintain a portfolio of three or four practices. Soil improving practices complement one another, whereas small scale irrigation substitutes for diversification and soil and pest management. Education, farm size, livestock ownership, and climatic exposure are associated with specific individual practices, while access to credit, extension services, and market information are associated with adoption across the portfolio. The findings highlight the important roles of institutional access and climate-related factors in the adoption of climate smart agricultural practices, particularly advisory services, credit access, and support for investment-intensive practices.

title: Diversifying GI systems through spatial bricolage: An empirical investigation of Italian wine farms
abstract: Geographical Indications (GIs) are crucial instruments for anchoring food quality to local territories. However, GI supply chains face growing environmental, market, and structural uncertainties, making the "reproduction" phase of the GI virtuous circle essential for long-term sustainability. This study investigates how GI wine farms in Italy implement extended territorial strategies through farm diversification and innovation, interpreted through the conceptual lens of spatial bricolage. Drawing on microdata from 11,720 GI wine holdings from the 7th Italian General Census of Agriculture, we deploy a multivariate statistical framework combining Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis (CA). Our findings identify three distinct farm typologies: (1) Traditionally Diversified, Non-Innovative Farms (46.8%), characterized by small scale, older managers, low digital adoption, and reliance on single-activity diversification; (2) Highly Innovative and Digitally Advanced Farms with Portfolio Strategies (17.0%), representing large farms with complex diversification portfolios; and (3) Diversified, Selectively Innovative and Moderately Digitalized Farms (36.2%), exhibiting pragmatic, incremental innovation and off-farm service provision. The results reveal heterogeneous configurations of farm diversification and innovation within GI systems, which can be interpreted as consistent with different forms of spatial bricolage. Accordingly, policy support may need to move beyond uniform measures and recognise differentiated structural, diversification, and innovation profiles when supporting the reproduction of GI wine systems.

title: Study on the coupling coordination relationship between agricultural and rural modernization and greening from a county-level perspective in Jilin Province, China
abstract: Exploring the coupling coordination between agricultural and rural modernization (ARM) and agricultural and rural greening (ARG) is of strategic importance for ensuring both China’s food security and ecological sustainability. This study developed a comprehensive indicator system to evaluate the development levels of ARM and ARG. Taking 14 key counties in Jilin Province as a case study, the entropy-weighted TOPSIS method was employed to evaluate the ARM and ARG levels from 2012 to 2022. The spatiotemporal coordination was analyzed using a coupling coordination degree model and spatial autocorrelation analysis.
